descriptor: LV/MV electrical panels and data-centre switchboards (NSE SME)
lede: A Navi Mumbai panel builder, licensed by ABB, whose data-centre switchboards went from 5% to half of revenue in two years, lifting EBITDA margin from 9% to 23%. A plant that roughly triples capacity starts this month; the risks are customer concentration, slow-paying receivables, dealings with promoter-owned firms, and a company that holds no earnings calls.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue +29% to ₹200 Cr, EBITDA margin 23% and PAT ₹32 Cr; H2 FY26 ₹130 Cr at 25%. Data centres (70% hyperscale) were ₹100 Cr of revenue, the executable order book is ₹205 Cr, and a 120,000 sq ft automated plant at Ambernath should start by end-October 2026.

Receivable days jumped to 213 and free cash flow was –₹26 Cr in FY26; 92% of revenue comes from Maharashtra and half from a few data-centre projects. ₹13 Cr of purchases and sales ran through firms owned by the promoters, one of which Vivid then bought from them; there is no earnings call.
~48x trailing earnings and ~35x EV/EBITDA, against RMC Switchgears at 10x, S&S Power at 44x and Marine Electricals at 103x.

blocks.text: Vivid designs, builds, tests and commissions low-voltage (up to 1,000 V) and medium-voltage (3.3-33 kV) switchboards and control panels: PCC, MCC, VFD, APFC and DG-synchronising panels, VCB and RMU panels, and data-centre PDUs. Most LV panels use ABB's licensed ArTu K design; it is also an ABB MV system integrator, a Siemens SIEPAN licensee and an L&T/Schneider accredited builder.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Vivid has ridden Mumbai's data-centre boom to high margins and is tripling capacity. The price assumes the new plant fills quickly at today's margins; concentration, rising receivables and related-party dealings mean investors should see H1 FY27 numbers and the plant running before paying up.
